misconceptions.statement: The pupil gives an estimate without considering a reasonable unit or benchmark size.
The pupil reads the hour and minute hands as if they use the same scale.
The pupil counts clock labels or subtracts visible digits without reasoning about duration.
The pupil assumes all months contain the same number of days.
The pupil compares the number of coins or notes instead of their total value.
The pupil does not connect change to the difference between amount paid and cost.
The pupil confuses the space inside a solid with the area of its outer surfaces.
The pupil multiplies three dimensions mechanically without connecting the product to layers of unit cubes or cubic units.
